verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_jump_analyzer_example_video: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Constants are well named and the module docstring explains the approach. Business logic uses single-letter or cryptic names: `d`, `m`, `n`, `k`, `f`, `fc`, `sm`, `nb`, `cand`. `detect_jump` and `athlete_bottoms` have no docstring explaining the run, peak and ground walk.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: Split into read_frames / athlete_bottoms / detect_jump / main, with no debug windows. `detect_jump` is about 70 lines doing run grouping, smoothing, peak finding and both walks. A generated `output.toml` was committed. `detect_jump` calls `athlete_bottoms` itself, so detection and segmentation are coupled.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Thresholds are named constants with rationale, and empty frames and NaN gaps are guarded. There is no `cap.isOpened()` check and no exception handling. An unreadable video or no detection silently produces `0, 0` (`if not present: return 0, 0`).

items.name: Robust to bad inputs and missing detections
items.name_zh: 异常输入与检测失败的处理
items.evidence: No `cap.isOpened()` check. An unreadable file or no detection writes `takeoff, landing = 0, 0` and exits 0, i.e. fake output. Uses absolute pixel constants fitted to the example: `HURDLE_X = 490`, `MIN_BOTTOM_Y = 150`, `DIFF_THRESH = 40`, `LANDING_TOL = 25`.

items.name: Output contract honoured
items.evidence: Reads argv[1] and writes `/app/output.toml` by default with exactly the two int fields. Without an argument it falls back to `/app/example_video.mp4`, and argv[2] can change the output path. Frames are numbered from 0 (enumerate), which is never stated. The hidden test failed, possibly due to the numbering convention or detection error.
